questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of Yemen?

hints.nudge: An official language is the one used in schools, courts and government. The other three are spoken in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “History” part of the Yemen article.

questions.prompt: What money is used in Yemen?

hints.nudge: Money names often come from a country’s own words. The other three are spent in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the part of the article about the economy, or at the facts for the country.

questions.proof: The money used in Yemen is the Yemeni rial.

questions.prompt: True or false: “Yemen shares a land border with Iran.”

hints.nudge: Read the statement slowly. Does it match what the article says, or has one word been swapped for another?
hints.whereToLook: Look at the Atlas and see which countries touch it.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries covers the most ground?

hints.nudge: Area is how much ground a country covers, not how many people live there. A small crowded country can still be small.
hints.whereToLook: Compare the four on the Atlas. Area means how much ground a country covers.

questions.proof: By area: Yemen about 455,503 square kilometres; Oman about 309,500 square kilometres; United Arab Emirates about 83,600 square kilometres; Israel about 20,770 square kilometres.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Yemen?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Yemen on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Yemen article.

questions.proof: It borders Saudi Arabia and Oman on the north and the east.
